summary: The prepared source already contains the issue-specific fix from upstream PR #33875 (merge commit 914644e81c9b6fc31d60a1ab5327a4884514c074): fused 2-D LoRA-B weights are sliced independently per logical merged section for each TP rank, while stacked 3-D adapters retain their established slicing. The legacy implementation reproduced the reported IndexError; the current implementation and its pre-existing regression passed.

tests.what_was_measured: Eleven focused fused-LoRA tests, including the pre-existing two-rank unequal-section regression against an independent unfused numerical reference.

On the assigned gfx950 GPU, the legacy slicer raised the reported 3-D-on-2-D IndexError; the current slicer returned exact expected rows for TP ranks 0 and 1 with unequal Q/K/V sections, and preserved exact 3-D stacked slicing at both rank boundaries.

gpu_evidence: reports/j-0a86e187342c/raw/gpu_lora_sharding.txt records exact-value assertions and synchronization on AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950).
remaining_limitations: MiniMax-H3 and Turbo LoRA weights were not available, so no full model semantic or video-generation validation was performed.

Only one assigned AMD gfx950 GPU was available; the reported two-rank behavior was exercised deterministically by mocking rank while all tensor operations ran on that GPU, not by a real multi-process collective.
The reporter used NVIDIA sm_120 hardware and TP=2; hardware-specific serving behavior on that platform remains unverified.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
